analysis.title: AI, Copper, and Geopolitics - GS Daily Monitor
key_insights: US equities opened the week lower, led by AI-related names, ahead of this week's AI earnings. NVDA reports Tuesday and BABA Thursday.
Copper fell to a 4-month low as tech shares sold off and Chinese economic data came in weaker.
Crude oil declined on signs the physical market is well supplied, despite tensions in the Middle East.
EU gas dropped as much as 6.2% as thin winter inventories were weighed against record US exports. EU gas storage has been a concern this year amid the Iran conflict.
Thailand Q3 GDP grew +2.9% against expectations of +3.1%. AI exports lifted growth while consumption and tourism stayed soft.
India CPI came in hot, which renews the risk of RBI tightening.
Ukraine hit the Crimean Bridge in a record drone strike on Russia overnight.
Bahrain said it intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks on Sunday, with the IRGC targeting a US radar site.
Zelensky said US envoys asked whether Ukraine would accept ceding Donbas to Russia in exchange for NATO membership.
Over the past week the 30y China government bond yield rose 7bp and the 10y CDB-CGB spread widened, on concerns about a potential bond tax change (GS EM Marketstrats).
earnings_insights: NVDA is scheduled to report earnings Tuesday (17 Nov 2026) and BABA Thursday (19 Nov 2026). The note gives no consensus figures for either.
